video_title_guess: Wemby's Dirty Play & Knicks Sweep: NBA Playoff Controversies & Draft Lottery Reactions

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.quote: If you're the best player on the team, he actually cost them this game. So, like, you have to hold him accountable the same way that we hold guys accountable whether they have a reputation for it or not. It was a dirty play, and it ended up costing them the game because they didn't have rim protection. They held up, Luke Kornet held it up as long as he could until that ran out, and then these guys started attacking the rim. He's got to be able to control his emotions more, especially in a pivotal game where they can possibly go up 3-1 going back to their home court. Instead, they're going back tied up in a pivotal three-game series that they got to fight through, and they're uncertain whether he's even going to play in Game 5. Seen if it's going to be a suspension.
quotes.why_it_matters: Lou Williams argues that Victor Wembanyama's flagrant foul was a 'bonehead play' that directly cost the Spurs a pivotal playoff game, emphasizing the need for accountability regardless of a player's reputation.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.quote: You can't put yourself in this situation as Victor Wembanyama, as the engine of this team, to get yourself tossed out of a game. He cost his team this game. He is too valuable, his impact just being out there alone, let alone his impact on the defensive end, the way he scores the basketball. Think about what he did Game 3 offensively with 39. He can't do things like this in such a critical moment in a critical series against a team, by the way, that is scrappy and that is not going away. You can't put yourself in this situation to do that. I hope he doesn't get suspended Game 5 because this is the hell of a series, and I don't think it was that. He's got no priors, he's got no history of doing this. Do not suspend him Game 5. This series is the best series, pretty much the only good series we got left.
quotes.why_it_matters: Chandler Parsons criticizes Victor Wembanyama for his ejection, stating that as the team's 'engine,' he cannot make such costly mistakes in a critical playoff series, though he hopes a suspension is avoided.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.quote: I'll be honest with you, maybe not a popular opinion, but I think you get a real look at Caleb Wilson. Drawing so many different comparisons from some of the great players in the game, from the Tim Duncans to the Kevin Garnetts to the KDs. He's getting a lot of different comparisons to the great players. Obviously we know AJ Dybantsa and his connections to Utah and them wanting him to be there. So them sitting at that number two pick, if I'm the Utah Jazz, I'm doing everything I can to get the Washington Wizards on the phone and see how we can see this through and make sure we get our guy and make sure you get your guy. But if I'm the Washington Wizards, I'm playing hardball because I know how bad the Utah Jazz want AJ at that number two spot. So I'm playing hardball because it can, I'm playing with house money now. I have an opportunity to go get a very talented player that can change the trajectory of my organization either way it goes, whether it's going to be Caleb Wilson or Peterson. There's so many different guys in this draft that can change your organization. But everybody knows the elephant in the room is the Utah Jazz wants AJ Dybantsa. We all know that. So with Washington, I'm playing hardball. What you got for me? If you want him to still be available at number two, what you got for me?
quotes.why_it_matters: Lou Williams advises the Wizards to play 'hardball' with the Jazz over the #1 draft pick, leveraging Utah's strong interest in AJ Dybantsa to maximize their return and accelerate their rebuild.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.quote: It's a unique draft because those top three, top four guys, even exclude Boozer because we kind of know what he's going to be, but the star potential power with Dybantsa, Peterson, and Wilson, it's tough because you don't really know who's going to be the best player. There's no Cooper Flagg, there's no Anthony Edwards, there's no for sure thing. I think the safest bet for the Wizards is taking AJ number one because you don't really want to take a risk with the number one pick if you're the Wizards right now. Caleb Wilson, as good as he is, I remember hitting the chatter when North Carolina's last game, the kid could be unbelievable, but that's a risk taking him with the number one pick. That's how you get fired if it doesn't pan out and work. So I think the ideal the number one pick is AJ. I know Ryan Smith and Utah, they love him. I don't know if they're going to work on a package to try and facilitate that, but I'm happy for the Wizards because this has been a horrible organization to call a spade a spade. They haven't had good luck, they haven't had many good years. And now at least they have this roster going forward with vet talent with Trae Young and Anthony Davis, who I think that's another interesting piece. You can move him on because he doesn't seem like he really wants to be there, but now you add AJ to the fold with Trae Johnson, with they have talent. There's something to look forward to with this team. I think they got to go AJ unless they kind of make a trade or a move.
quotes.why_it_matters: Chandler Parsons suggests the Wizards should make the 'safest bet' by drafting AJ Dybantsa with the #1 pick, given the uncertainty of other top prospects and the franchise's need for a foundational piece.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.quote: Being honest with yourself and where you are in your career, how much time do I have left? Do I want to become sort of this veteran leadership type of guy where I'm the head of the snake along with Trae Young, and we bring these young guys along and see what we can do? Or do I kind of force my way out and say, 'Hey, look, young guys, y'all got it, y'all can figure this thing out. I only got X amount of years left. I'm trying to compete for championships.' So I can see it both ways. I can't read his mind, and I haven't seen him make a statement as of yet. But I'm kind of 50/50 where I am with AD and staying in Washington because I can see it in both sides. He's been to the mountaintop, he's gotten a championship. If you got one, you want another one, and I don't think they get it in Washington right away. In the next few years that they're there, they can build towards that area, but there's some other situations that are already made for him already.
quotes.why_it_matters: Lou Williams speculates on Anthony Davis's career crossroads, questioning whether he'll embrace a veteran leadership role with the Wizards or seek a trade to a ready-made championship contender.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.quote: This was one of the biggest losers ever. And I love the fact that Kevin Pritchard came out and he owned up to it, and he took accountability. He said, 'Listen, we swung for the fences, we lost.' He took a risk. Regardless, we still needed a starting center, which Zubac is a great piece for them. And think about it, this is basically that same team that made a run to the finals without Miles Turner but insert Zoo, and they lose Benedict Mathurin. Now again, when you have this draft that's so top-heavy and they could have got a great pick, and if it was just one to four or 10 to 30 to keep it, and it fell to the worst possible situation for this, and the best possible situation for the Clippers. If you think it's rigged or whatever, now the Clippers get rewarded for everything he did last year. This was a bad beat, and again, this kind of serves him right because they purposely tried to lose and they tanked all year long, so I'm kind of glad they didn't get rewarded, but also this sucks. And this was a team that you put a top four pick on that existing team with Tyrese Haliburton back, with Siakam, with those guys, the same team that went to the finals with a top four pick, it would have been a dream, but man, what a nightmare.
quotes.why_it_matters: Chandler Parsons criticizes the Pacers' front office for their trade involving Ivica Zubac, which resulted in them losing a top-4 protected draft pick, calling it a 'nightmare' scenario that backfired spectacularly.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.quote: I do respect the fact that the GM came out and he owned it. He got ahead of that train before it left the station. Very smart. 'Hey, listen, that one's on me. I thought we were doing some luck. It didn't pan out. But remember, we needed this player. We needed this guy. So let's keep it all in perspective what we needed.' And he got, he got ahead of it, and that way you can still have the support of your community and your organization to move forward with you knowing that, 'Hey, this is going to be our group moving forward, ain't no help coming.' I wish people would learn from that, right? And poor Tyrese is coming back. He has the potential to do so. And poor Tyrese is coming back. Everybody want a little fresh energy, some new blood in the building to push things along, but the reality is he's going to have to be that fresh blood and energy. What they traded for Zubac, I love me some Zubac, but good lord, the picks. If we're talking, if we're talking players, I like Ben Mathurin. Isaiah Jackson is somebody that's going to figure it out. But Zubac is a player, Zubac is a hooper. Mathurin is a 20 ball, and the fifth pick is like Cam Boozer. That's tough. It was a loss, they were the losers of the day. More than the Sixers? I don't know. It's a lot. I love me some Zuchi man, you know. He should feel real good about himself. And again, they needed a center anyways, but not at that clip. No, it's very, very expensive.
quotes.why_it_matters: Lou Williams praises the Pacers' GM for taking accountability for the Zubac trade, highlighting the importance of transparency and managing expectations within the organization despite the unfavorable outcome.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.quote: I think the Knicks have been one of the best teams in the postseason, if we're being honest. Whatever they were saying about, you distract me. You got to give credit where it's due, man. I thought, I thought New York Knicks, they played great in the first round. How they closed out Atlanta was a statement, and what they just did to Philadelphia was another statement. You got to give them credit where it's due. They're playing lights out, and they're getting it from, from every angle, from everybody. It looks like everybody's just bought into the mission. We were calling for Mike Brown to be fired a month ago, and here we are, and they're playing genius level basketball. Philly just didn't show up in the second round. I think they exerted too much energy with trying to get out of the first round against Boston, being down 3-1, and just never showing up to the fight against, against the New York Knicks. So this team is absolutely rolling. I'll probably say they might be the best team left in the postseason right now, with the Thunder included, based on a 50-point win to close out in a Game 7, and a sweep in Round 2. If this was the Thunder with those same stats, we'd have gave him a ring already.
quotes.why_it_matters: Lou Williams asserts the Knicks are playing 'lights out' and are potentially the best team left in the playoffs, praising their decisive wins against the Hawks and 76ers.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.quote: They're playing unbelievable basketball. They're getting more productive. And this is without OG, who's been their second best player in the postseason. I don't think that's a long-term thing that he's out, but Bridges was great. McBride, Deuce was great. They're getting production from their bench, which we haven't said in years from the New York Knicks. And I think the only reason that we were, at least I was hesitant on the Knicks in their original series is the Atlanta Hawks were the hottest team in the NBA. They were playing such good basketball. I thought that could be a bad matchup for the Knicks, and they handled it. And obviously it was a tough series, but they got out of that. Philly against Boston just looked like the better team. They looked the more complete team, and then they just looked like a completely different team against the Knicks. And you have to give the Knicks credit. They exposed them, they took out their weaknesses. They were more efficient. When you shoot the three ball like this, it's hard to lose games, and they just were dominant. Jalen Brunson was fantastic. Cat is playing with a sense of urgency that we've wanted him to play with all season long. So again, are they a title contender? I still think the title, the champs come out of the West, and probably going to be OKC. Spurs now are in a dogfight. I still think the Spurs are the second best team in the playoffs, but the Knicks you can't overlook what they're doing and how they're playing. And when they're getting this production from their bench, and Jalen Brunson's efficient, and Cat is playing with a motor, Mikal Bridges is scoring the basketball now like he did in the first series, they are a more complete balanced team than they've ever been, and they look really, really good right now.
quotes.why_it_matters: Chandler Parsons highlights the Knicks' improved bench production, efficient three-point shooting, and strong individual performances from Jalen Brunson and others as reasons for their dominant playoff run.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.quote: I want to go back to Mike Brown and coaching. You got to give New York credit because their game plan was, was ironclad. Their plan was, we're going to make Kelly Oubre beat us. We're going to throw, we're going to throw two guys at Maxey, we're going to throw two guys at Embiid, we're going to rotate off of everybody, we're going to leave Kelly Oubre open. And for a while he made him pay. Game before last he had 20 plus points. He was making him play from the three, but if that's the guy that's going to have to beat you on the offensive end, if I'm New York, I feel really good about that and keeping the ball out of Tyrese Maxey and Embiid's hands. And then you come back in that next game, you have some success with that, and you go do it again, and you get, you get another big 30-point win to move on to the next round. So you got to give credit where's due. The New York Knicks played lights out, but you got to give credit to Mike Brown as well for having a great game plan.
quotes.why_it_matters: Lou Williams praises the Knicks' coaching staff for their 'ironclad' game plan against the 76ers, specifically highlighting their strategy to force Kelly Oubre Jr. to beat them offensively while limiting Tyrese Maxey and Joel Embiid.

quotes.speaker: Michelle Beadle
quotes.quote: Is it weird that the one close game was the one that Joel Embiid didn't play in? Like it just felt like it was a completely different situation because this did not look like even close to what we watched play Boston. It was just tough to have him in and out of the lineup, Round 1 and Round 2, because you are dealing with a runaway train in the New York Knicks. They were rolling. If you win a game seven by 50 plus points, my confidence is sky high. And so now I feel good about my game plan. I feel good about how we're playing as a team, we're confident, we're ready to roll, we're motivated. And for Philly to not kind of have any consistency in what they were doing, no stability is a better word for that. They didn't have the stability in and ever having opportunity to really get and and get it, be a part of this, this series in a real competitive way. And New York Knicks, they took full advantage of it. So I wouldn't say that it was weird that the close game was the one that Joel Embiid was out. It's just tough to play that way when you don't have stability, and you're looking down a barrel at a team that's ready to roll against any team.
quotes.why_it_matters: Michelle Beadle points out the irony that the 76ers' only close game against the Knicks was when Joel Embiid was absent, suggesting his inconsistent availability disrupted team stability and rhythm.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.quote: I don't think they run it back as this team is constructed. I think now it's very clear this is a Tyrese Maxey-led team, but logic tells me they're not going to be able to get rid of this contract, especially if you can't keep Joel Embiid on the floor more than 38 games. If you're going to sign up for that, I'm going to want 50 to 55, even upwards of 60 games out of this if they figured it out. So, I think he did a great job in controlling the narrative, controlling the message when it comes to, to his knee going into an offseason where he doesn't know what the future holds. So great job in doing that. But I don't think they run it back as constructed if they can find a trade partner. But logic tells me different. Unfortunately, this always happens with a lot of players towards the end of their career, and there's always those conversations of a buyout of getting the contract stretched or something like that. And again, that's going to have to be a conversation that they have internally and individually. But it's a tough team-friendly contract because that is a lot of money from a guy that you just don't know how many games he's going to play. We know how great he is when he's healthy. He's just not really healthy, and he's not getting younger. So that is the problem for them.
quotes.why_it_matters: Lou Williams believes the 76ers cannot run back their current roster, arguing that Joel Embiid's contract is too burdensome given his injury history and limited games played, suggesting Tyrese Maxey should lead the team instead.
